subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Hoover Dam: Taming the Colorado
description: A quick, practical guide to The Hoover Dam: Taming the Colorado.

hook.text: The Hoover Dam contains enough concrete to build a two-lane highway from San Francisco to New York.

buildup.text: Workers diverted the Colorado River through tunnels, then poured concrete 24 hours a day for 2 years.

discovery.text: If poured as one block, the concrete would take 125 years to cool. Engineers used interlocking columns.

twist.text: 96 workers died during construction. The first death and last death were a father and son, 13 years apart.

climax.text: The dam powers 1.3 million homes and irrigates farmland that feeds millions across the Southwest.

punchline.text: They poured enough concrete to pave a continent.

quiz.question: Why couldn't the Hoover Dam's concrete be poured as one single block?
options: The weight would have cracked the canyon walls beneath it
It would have taken 125 years to cool and would crack
No pump existed that could deliver that much concrete
